# Edva Language Guide & Extended Reference (llms-full.txt)

> This document contains a curated language reference, grammar rules, operational semantics,
> operator tables, and standard library guide for the Edva programming language (`edva`),
> formatted for ingestion by Large Language Models and AI coding agents. Complete, maintained
> module-by-module documentation is available in the Quarto reference at `doc/reference/stdlib/`.

---

# 1. Core Principles & Hard Rules

- **Zero Bare Keywords**: Words such as `if`, `else`, `for`, `while`, `fn`, `return`,
  `continue`, `import`, and `break` are ordinary identifiers with no special syntactic
  meaning. Control flow is unified into symbolic expressions.
- **No RTTI, Ever**: Types are fully erased at runtime. Function values are `{ fn_ptr, env_ptr }`
  closures. All polymorphism and function types are statically verified and resolved.
- **Integer Literals & No Defaulting to Int**:
  - Unsuffixed integer literals evaluate to the current default integer type (`Int` by default,
    or as configured by `#pragma number <type>`).
  - No Defaulting to Int: The type system never silently coerces ambiguous expressions or
    unresolved type variables to `Int`. Ambiguous or unknowable types must be annotated explicitly
    or produce a compile-time error (`E3103`).
- **Binary Comparisons**: Comparison operators are `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`, `!<`, and `!>`.
  - Greater-than-or-equal is written as `!<` (reads as "greater or equal").
  - Less-than-or-equal is written as `!>` (reads as "less or equal").
  - `>=` and `<=` do NOT exist in the language.
  - On floating-point values, `!<` and `!>` are ordered comparisons (LLVM `OGE` / `OLE`). If either
    operand is NaN, the comparison evaluates to false (`<->`). This is distinct from logical
    negation: for NaN `x`, `x !< 1.0` is false, while `!(x < 1.0)` is true.
- **Binding Mutability**: Edva uses `=` uniformly for bindings and reassignments. Bindings are
  immutable by default. Rebindable local variables use trailing prime (`'`) identifiers
  (`x' = 1; x' = x' + 1`). Parameters are strictly immutable. Interior mutations (`pt.x = 1`,
  `arr += 1`, `b += "x"`) do not require primed bindings.
- **Clean Choices**: A single-branch choice `cond | action` evaluates as a statement. Never supply
  dummy `| 0` fallbacks in statement positions.
- **Unquoted Imports**: Module imports use bare identifiers: `#use net`, `#use io`, `#use libc`.
- **Indentation & Line Length**: Code uses consistent space-only indentation. Line lengths must
  not exceed 100 characters.

---

# 2. Lexical Structure

## 2.1 Identifiers & Keywords
Identifiers conform to UAX31. Edva has zero bare keywords. Directives start with `#`:
- `#use`: imports a module (`#use net`, `#use str`).
- `#type`: declares a nominal record, ram, or enum type (`#type Point (x: Int, y: Int)`).
- `#foreign`: declares foreign C ABI functions (`#foreign "c"`).
- `#public` / `#private`: access visibility directives.
- `#!`: compile-time evaluation.
- `#pragma number <type>`: switches default integer literal type (`i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `default`).

## 2.2 Literals
- **Integers**: Decimal (`42`), Hexadecimal (`0x2A`), Binary (`0b101010`), Octal (`0o755`), Repeating (`0b1{4}`, `10{6}`, `0b1{48}`).
  Limits: `0max`, `0min` (with optional suffixes: `0maxu64`, `0mini32`).
  Explicit type suffixes: `5i16`, `0xFFu8`, `100u32`, `9i64`, `0b1{32}u32`.
- **Floats**: `3.14`, `0.5`, `1.0e-5`. Built-in FP constants: `-.0` (negative zero), `.inf`, `-.inf` (infinities),
  `.nan` (quiet NaN), `.max`, `-.max` (finite bounds), `.min` (minimal positive normal), `.sub` (minimal positive subnormal),
  with optional suffixes (`.nanf32`, `.maxf32`, `-.0f32`). Dangling dots (`.5`, `1.`) are illegal.
- **Runes**: Single Unicode codepoints: `'a'`, `'🔥'`, `'\n'`.
- **Strings**:
  - Escaped & Unified: `"hello\nworld"` or multiline `"\n    line 1\n    line 2\n    "`.
    Supports margin stripping when starting with `"\n`, line continuation `\`,
    and `${expr}` dynamic interpolation for scalar primitives (lowered via the `%to_str`
    intrinsic without requiring `#use str`). Triple-quote `"""` is retired.
- **Repetition**: `expr {N}` generates a record containing `N` flat copies of `expr`
  (e.g., `0 {8}` produces `(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)`).
- **Builder Literal**: `{expr}` starting an expression creates a mutable Builder buffer with
  initial capacity `expr` (e.g., `{64}`).

---

# 3. Operators & Precedence Table

The operator precedence hierarchy is organized into binding tiers (from loosest to tightest):

<!-- BEGIN operators.yaml -->
| Tier | LBP | RBP | Operators | Associativity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cycle | 10 | 20 | `@` `@@` `>--` `-->` `--^` | left |
| sequence | 20 | 30 | `;` | left |
| apply | 30 | 30 | `$` `$:` | right |
| feed | 40 | 50 | `$>` `$>>` | left |
| choice | 50 | 60 | `|` `[pattern]` `!|` `|->` `|+>` `|-->` `|++>` | left |
| assignment | 60 | 50 | `=` `:=` `+=` `::=` | right |
| range | 70 | 80 | `..` | left |
| logical or | 80 | 90 | `||` | left |
| logical and | 90 | 100 | `&&` | left |
| bitwise or | 100 | 105 | `.|.` | left |
| bitwise xor | 105 | 110 | `.^.` | left |
| bitwise and | 110 | 120 | `.&.` | left |
| comparison | 120 | 130 | `<` `>` `==` `!=` `!<` `!>` | left, same-line |
| shift | 130 | 140 | `.<.` `.>.` | left |
| addition | 140 | 150 | `+` `-` | left |
| multiplication | 150 | 160 | `*` `/` `%` | left |
| unary prefix | 160 | 180 | `!` `+` `&` `++` `.!.` `~~` `?` `??` `-x` `#size` | right |
| postfix / apply | 170 | 180 | `call ()` `.` `::` `: cast` `{N}` `@[...]` `!!` `--!` | left |
| primary | 180 | 180 | `primary` | left |

<!-- END operators.yaml -->

Notable precedence facts:
- `$>` (feed) and `$` (infix apply) sit below the choice tier:
  `f(a) $ b` == `f(a, b)` (append), `x $> f(a)` == `f(x, a)` (prepend).
  `$>` is left-associative, `$` is right-associative.
- Postfix `--!` (error propagation) sits in the postfix / apply tier (tier 18).
- Cycle jumps (`-->`, `--^`) and cycle escape (`>--`) sit in the cycle tier (tier 1).
- Bitwise precedence is C-style: `||` < `&&` < `.|.` < `.&.` < comparison < `.<.` `.>.`
  < `+` `-` < `*` `/` `%`.

---

# 4. Control Flow: Choices & Cycles

## 4.1 Choice Expressions
Choices replace `if`, `switch`, and pattern matching. A choice consists of a scrutinee, an
ordered chain of guarded branches, and an optional fallback:
```dva complete
classify: Int => String
classify = score =>
   score [100]       "perfect"
         [> 89]      "distinction"
         [> 49]      "pass"
         |           "fail"
```

- **Guards**:
  - `[val]`: Equality test (`x [target]` == `x == target`).
  - `[1, 2, 3]`: Comma-separated value OR-list (matches if `x` equals any item).
  - `[> 89]`: Operator section predicate comparison.
  - `[Variant]`: Unit enum variant match (or payload-ignoring match; `[Variant _]` is disallowed).
  - `[V1, V2]`: Multi-variant OR guard.
  - `[Variant payload]`: Tagged enum variant payload binding (space-separated juxtaposition without parentheses; parentheses introduce a nested tuple/record subpattern such as `[Add (a, b)]`; construct enums with `Enum(Variant)` or `Enum(Variant, payload)`).
- **Statement Choices**: Single-branch choices without fallbacks evaluate for side effects:
```dva partial reason="statement choice fragment"
has_error | log("Error detected")
```

## 4.2 Cycles & Control
Iteration is performed using `@`:
```dva partial reason="cycle jump fragment"
// Iterate over an integer range (0 to count-1)
0..count @ i =>
   i [2] --^         // --^ skips this iteration (continue)
   i [8] -->         // --> terminates the loop (break)
   io::out $ i
```

Multi-level jumps support integer suffixes: `-->2` breaks out of two enclosing loops.

## 4.3 Cycle Escapes (`>--`)
Appending `>-- BranchBody` turns a cycle into an expression returning `RamPN` `< T | >`:
- If the cycle breaks via `-->`, the branch evaluates and returns `<+ branch_value +>`.
- If the cycle completes normally without breaking, the result is `<-->` (negative unit):
```dva complete
find_target: Int, Int => < Int | >
find_target = count, target =>
   0..count @ i =>
      i [target] -->
   >--
      target
```

## 4.4 Early Return (`--|`)
Functions exit early using `--|`:
- `--| value`: Returns `value` immediately; must match the function's declared return type.
- Bare `--|`: Early return from a void function (`() => ()`).

```dva complete
clamp: Int, Int, Int => Int
clamp = x, lo, hi =>
   x < lo | --| lo
   x > hi | --| hi
   x
```

## 4.5 Ram Branch Return Sugars
Choice branches can return unit ramifications directly from an enclosing function:
- `cond |->` desugars to `cond | --| <->` (`RamNN` `<>` Flag negative / false)
- `cond |+>` desugars to `cond | --| <+>` (`RamNN` `<>` Flag positive / true)
- `cond |-->` desugars to `cond | --| <-->` (`RamPN` `< T | >` negative unit / absence)
- `cond |++>` desugars to `cond | --| <++>` (`RamNP` `< | E >` positive unit / success)

```dva complete
find_positive: Int => < Int | >
find_positive = n =>
   n !> 0 |-->
   <+ n +>
```

---

# 5. Type System & Algebraic Ramifications

## 5.1 Primitive Types
- `Int`: Fixed 64-bit signed integer (`i64`) on all architectures (no `isize`/`usize`).
- `Float`: 64-bit IEEE 754 floating point (`double`).
- `String`: Immutable UTF-8 fat pointer `{ i64 len, i8* data }`.
- `Builder`: Mutable byte buffer `{ i64 len, i8* data, i64 cap }*`.
- `Rune`: 32-bit Unicode scalar value (`i32`).
- `Addr`: Raw memory address (architecture-dependent: 4 bytes on 32-bit, 8 bytes on 64-bit). Casts via `Addr(...)` are strictly restricted to integerish types (`Int`, `i8`..`u64`) and pointers. Memory addresses of strings, builders, records, and call-argument scalars are obtained via `&`.
- `Flag`: Bare boolean (`i1`), constructed with `<+>` (true) or `<->` (false).
- `Error`: Standard error record `(code: Int, msg: String, file: String, line: Int, col: Int, context: (Int, Int))`.

## 5.2 The Four Ramification Shapes & Constructors
Ramifications represent binary outcomes with zero-cost runtime representations:
1. `RamNN` (`<>`): Bare `i1` Flag.
   - Positive constant: `<+>`
   - Negative constant: `<->`
2. `RamPN` (`< T | >`): Option / value presence. Positive carries `T`; negative carries unit `()`.
   - Positive constructor: `<+ val +>`
   - Negative unit constant: `<-->`
3. `RamNP` (`< | E >`): Success or error payload. Positive carries unit `()`; negative carries `E`.
   - Positive unit constant: `<++>`
   - Negative constructor: `<- err ->`
4. `RamPP` (`< T | E >`): Two-payload result. Unboxed register aggregate `{ i1 tag, i64 payload }`.
   - Positive constructor: `<+ val ->`
   - Negative constructor: `<- err +>`

Payload constructors close with `+>` or `->` (never bare `>`). Single-payload rams with
pointer payloads (`String`, `Record`) use null-pointer niche optimization (`ptr`, where null
is absence/unit, 0 extra tag bits). In `RamPP`, the `i1 tag` is a runtime polarity discriminant
(not RTTI; types are fully erased). The four shapes are distinct static types with incompatible
representations; there is no implicit coercion between them.

In expression position, an inexhaustive choice whose non-jump branches all produce `RamPN`
(`< T | >`) or `RamNP` (`< | E >`) automatically synthesizes an implicit fallback branch:
`| <-->` for `RamPN` (absence) or `| <++>` for `RamNP` (success).

## 5.3 Monadic Bind (`$>>`) & Error Bubbling (`--!`)
- Monadic Bind (`$>>`): Left-associative bind over ramifications with a positive payload
  (`RamPP` or `RamPN`). Named functions receive the positive payload directly.
- Postfix Error Propagation (`--!`): Unwraps a positive payload inline or early-returns the
  negative error from the enclosing function:
  ```dva
  step_a: Int => < Int | String >
  step_a = x =>
     x < 0 | <- "negative" +> | <+ x * 2 ->

  step_b: Int => < Int | String >
  step_b = x =>
     x == 0 | <- "zero" +> | <+ 100 / x ->

  compute: Int, Int => < Int | String >
  compute = a, b =>
     v1 = step_a(a)--!
     v2 = step_b(b)--!
     <+ v1 + v2 ->
  ```

---

# 6. Memory Management: Strings & Builders

- Strings are immutable. String concatenation (`s1 + s2`) allocates a fresh string buffer.
- Builders provide high-throughput mutable buffering:
  - Allocation: `b = {128}` allocates initial buffer capacity.
  - In-place append: `b += "text"`, `b += 'A'`, or homogeneous records `b += (13, 10)`.
  - Freeze (`+b`): Consumes and resets the Builder descriptor, transferring the buffer pointer
    directly into an immutable String in place (allocating only the 16-byte String descriptor
    in the active arena without copying bytes).
  - Interop: `&b` yields the writable buffer address (`Addr`); `&s` yields the string data pointer; `&rec` yields a record/tuple pointer; `&scalar` yields a scalar address in call-argument position (e.g. FFI out-parameters); `?b = n` sets the active length after an external FFI read.

---

# 7. Hardware Acceleration & LLVM Intrinsics

Intrinsics are prefixed with `%` and lower directly into LLVM IR instructions:
- **Math**: `%min(a, b)`, `%max(a, b)`, `%clamp(val, min, max)`, `%abs(x)`, `%sqrt(x)`.
- **Saturating Arithmetic**: `%uadd_sat(a, b)`, `%usub_sat(a, b)`.
- **Vector Reductions**: `%sum(vec)`, `%prod(vec)`, `%dot(v1, v2)`.
- **Memory**: `%memcpy(dst, src, len)`, `%memmove(dst, src, len)`, `%memset(dst, val, len)`, `%ptrmask(ptr, mask)`.
- **String Conversion**: `%to_str(scalar)` converts scalar primitives (`Int`, `UInt`, `Float`, `Rune`, `String`) into an arena-allocated `String` (used as the underlying lowering for `"${expr}"` interpolation).

---

# 8. POSIX & Foreign Function Interface (FFI)

Foreign C symbols are declared under `#foreign "c"` with typed function signatures:
```dva complete
#foreign "c"
   open: (path: String, flags: Int) => Int
   close: (fd: Int) => Int
   read: (fd: Int, buf: Addr, count: Int) => Int

read_file: String => < String | >
read_file = path =>
   fd = open(path, 0)
   fd [< 0] <-->
   |
      b = {4096}
      n = read(fd, &b, 4096)
      close(fd)
      n > 0 | (?b = n; <+ +b +>) | <-->
```

---

# 9. Standard Library Overview & Module Contracts

Complete reference documentation for each module is maintained in `doc/reference/stdlib/`.

- **`io`**: Stream-based buffered reading (`Reader`, `read_line`, `read_all`) and console logging
  (`out`, `outs`, `err`, `errs`, `outf`, `errf`).
  - *Contract*: Output helpers (`out`, `outs`, `err`, `errs`, `outf`, `errf`) loop across partial transfers, retry on `EINTR`, and return `()`. Low-level `io::write(fd, s)` returns total bytes transferred (`Int`, or `-1` on initial error).
- **`fs`**: High-level safe filesystem operations, paths, directory traversal, and capacity stats.
  - *Functions*: `join`, `parent`, `basename`, `ext`, `is_abs`, `cwd`, `home`, `resolve`, `read_to_string`,
    `write_file`, `copy_file`, `rename_path`, `remove`, `remove_all`, `create_dir`, `create_dir_all`, `stat`,
    `lstat_meta`, `exists`, `is_file`, `is_dir`, `is_symlink`, `mtime`, `size`, `readlink_path`, `read_dir`,
    `list_dir`, `space`, `get_fs_stats`, `format_size`, `format_perms`, `format_time`, `format_number`,
    `auto_rename_path`.
  - *Contract*: Uses typed `#packed` records (`StatRaw`, `Statvfs`, `DirentPrefix`) and safe options `<T | >`.
- **`in`**: Singleton standard-input reader wrapping `stdin_r`.
  - *Functions*: `read_line(max)`, `read_bytes(max)`, `read_byte!`, `read_until(delim, max)`.
  - *Status*: `err!` (last errno), `eof!` (clean EOF), `would_block!` (`EAGAIN`), `has_err!`, `clear!`.
- **`str`**: Byte-oriented string predicates, scalar conversions, ordering, and digit parsing.
  - *Functions*: `from_byte`, `from_int`, `from_float`, `hex_to_str`, `to_int`, `to_hex`, `cmp`, `lt`, `is_digit`, `is_alpha`, `is_alnum`, `is_ws`, `is_hex`.
- **`unicode`** & **`utf`**: Unicode general category classification and UTF-8 rune encoding/decoding (`decode_rune`, `utf8_width`, `encode_rune`, `append_rune`).
- **`net` & `net/http`**: TCP networking and HTTP/1.1 protocol handling.
  - *Network*: `tcp_listen`, `tcp_accept`, `tcp_connect`, `send_str`, `recv`, `close_fd: Int => Int`.
  - *HTTP*: `read_request`, `path_of`, `header`, `response`, `respond(fd, status, content_type, body)`.
  - *Contract*: Request reading rejects unsupported `Transfer-Encoding`, enforces Content-Length bounds,
    and returns `Req(<- "incomplete body" +>)` on truncated payloads.
- **`json`**: Whole-document JSON parser (`json::parse: String => <Value | Error>`).
  - *Types*: `Value` (`String`, `Number`, `Boolean`, `Null`, `Array`, `Object`).
  - *Contract*: Uses module-global `::src`/`::pos` state; **not reentrant and not thread-safe**.
    Concurrent calls must be synchronized or run in separate processes. Raw strings are validated
    for strict UTF-8 (rejecting overlong encodings, invalid continuation/lead bytes, surrogate halves
    `0xD800`–`0xDFFF`, and out-of-range scalars). Numbers preserve compensated decimal exponents.
- **`sort`**: Collection sorting helpers.
  - *Functions*: `ints(Ints) => Ints` and `strings(Strings) => Strings` use hybrid merge sort
    ($O(n \log n)$) on array copies. `raw_sort_slots` uses callback-driven in-place insertion sort
    ($O(n^2)$) for small custom collections.
- **`math`**, **`math/geom`**, **`math/complex`**: Numerical and spatial operations.
  - *Scalars*: `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `sqrt`, `atan2`, `floor`, `ceil`, `fabs`, `ldexp`.
  - *Geometry*: `Vec2`, `Vec3`, `Vec4`, `Rect`, `dot`, `len`, `dist`, `norm`, `lerp`, `angle`, `rotate`, `rect_contains`, `circle_contains`, `rect_union`, `rect_intersect`.
  - *Complex*: `Complex`, `make`, `real`, `imag`, `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `abs`, `exp`, `fft`, `ifft`.
- **`event`**: Portable file descriptor readiness multiplexing backed by `poll(2)` (`Poller`, `Event`, `new!`, `add`, `mod`, `del`, `wait`, `close`).
- **`uring`**: Linux `io_uring` asynchronous I/O submission and completion queues (`new`, `prep_read`, `prep_write`, `submit`, `wait_cqe`, `reap`, `close`).
- **`color`** & **`color/palette`**: Color spaces (`Rgba`, `LinearRgba`, `Oklab`, `Oklch`, `Hsv`), hex packing (`from_hex`, `to_hex`, `from_hex_str`, `to_hex_str`), alpha blending (`alpha_blend`), perceptual interpolation (`lerp_oklab`), and theme palettes (`palette::Palette`).
- **`fp`**: Functional combinators over collections (`map`, `filter`, `fold`, `reduce`, `any`, `all`, `count`, `find`, `take`, `drop`, `reverse`, `zip`).
- **`type`**: Compile-time type predicates and numeric limits (`is_int`, `is_float`, `is_signed`, `is_unsigned`, `bit_width`, `min_val`, `max_val`).
- **`libc`**: Direct POSIX C system call bindings (`open`, `close`, `read`, `write`, `malloc`).
- **`mem`**: Memory management utilities and arena allocators.
- **`os`** & **`sys`**: Operating system environment, command-line arguments (`sys::argv`), and exits.
- **`ccl`**: Configuration file parsing for the CCL format (`ccl::parse`).

---

# 10. Compiler Diagnostic Reference

- `E2001`–`E2099`: Lexical and syntax parse errors.
- `E3004`: Undefined identifier or symbol.
- `E3008`: Negation `!` applied to non-Flag type (use `+b` for freeze, `!!` for unwrap).
- `E3033`: Reassignment to an unprimed immutable binding.
- `E3084`: Type unification failure (including invalid equality on non-enum ramifications).
- `E3089`: Incompatible ramification shapes in assignment or choice.
- `E3103`: Cannot infer concrete type for expression without RTTI.
- `E3130`–`E3132`: Field initialization tracking errors and compile-time evaluation failures.
- `E5001`–`E5011`: Driver, linker, and target compilation errors.
